title: (Modified) Jeff Nippard's Min-Max 5 Days
author: Agustín  M.
desc:
### Who is it for?
The *Min-Max* program is designed around the principles of low volume and maximum intensity, specifically targeting three types of people:
 1. *Athletes with limited time:* People looking for quick but highly effective workouts of about 45 minutes, 4 to 5 times a week.
 2. *High-intensity enthusiasts:* Lifters who prioritize quality over quantity and enjoy pushing each set to the absolute limit.
 3. *Cutting phases (Calorie Deficit):* Ideal for maintaining muscle mass and strength when the body’s energy resources are limited.

### Weekly Training Volume
To avoid unnecessary volume and ensure optimal recovery, the program drastically reduces the number of sets, requiring maximum effort (RIR 0-1) in each one instead:
 * *Chest, Shoulders, Upper Back, Lats, Biceps, Triceps, Forearms, Quadriceps, and Glutes:* Between *6 and 10 sets per week* in total.
 * *Hamstrings, Calves, and Abs:* *4 sets per week* in total.
 * Note: This translates to performing only *1 or 2 super-heavy working sets* per exercise in each session.

### Advanced Intensity Techniques
In Block 2 of the program, advanced techniques are introduced in the final set of exercises selected to push the muscle beyond failure:
 * *Drop Sets:* After reaching muscle failure, immediately reduce the weight by ~25% and train to failure again. Reduce the weight by another ~25% and go to failure one last time (3 consecutive sets without rest).
 * *Lengthened Partials:* Upon reaching failure through the full range of motion (ROM), continue performing partial reps only in the position where the muscle is most stretched until you can no longer move the weight.
 * *Myo-Reps:* After reaching failure in the normal set, rest for only 5 seconds and perform 2 reps. Repeat this mini-cycle (5-second rest + 2 reps) consecutively until you can no longer complete the 2 full reps.
 * *Weighted Static Hold:* Upon reaching failure on the bench press, hold the weight down (in the position of maximum stretch) while statically maintaining full tension for 30 seconds.

### Warm-Up Protocol (Sets and Reps)
Before starting, we recommend 5 minutes of light cardio to raise your body temperature. Afterward, perform specific warm-up sets based on the exercise in your routine:
 * *If the exercise calls for 1 warm-up set:* Use ~60% of your working weight to perform 6 to 10 fluid repetitions.
 * *If it calls for 2 warm-up sets:*
   * Set 1: ~50% of your working weight x 6–10 reps.
   * Set 2: ~70% of your working weight x 4–6 reps.
 * *If it calls for 3 warm-up sets:*
   * Set 1: ~45% of your working weight x 6–10 reps.
   * Set 2: ~65% of the working weight x 4–6 reps.
   * Set 3: ~85% of the working weight x 3–4 reps.
 * *If you do 4 warm-up sets:*
   * Set 1: ~45% of the working weight x 6–10 reps.
   * Set 2: ~60% of working weight x 4–6 reps.
   * Set 3: ~75% of working weight x 3–5 reps.
   * Set 4: ~85% of working weight x 2–4 reps.
